focus: Anchor nesting produced by the core spec template
noveltyJustification: Six of seven findings are fully new (template source lines, render effect, rule-3 prohibition, conditional rendering, scaffold pointer, creation-time path correctness); one confirms the operator hypothesis and counts as half new.
ruledOut: Fixing rendered packets without fixing the template

label: CONFIRMED at the template source: templates/core/spec.md.tmpl opens ANCHOR:questions at line 184, closes it at line 399 (level:1,2,3 path) with a second closer at line 425 (level:3+ path), so everything between renders inside the questions anchor.

The rendered Level 2 scaffold sample shows the nested result: questions opens at line 128, nfr pairs 132-146, edge-cases 150-166, complexity 170-179, questions closes at 187; three anchored sections live inside another anchored section.

ANCHORS_VALID rule 3 says anchors cannot contain other anchors, and its scope includes spec.md/plan.md/tasks.md/acceptance-criteria.md/decision-record.md/implementation-summary.md, so every newly scaffolded Level 2 or 3 packet starts life with an anchor violation.
The template selects level-specific sections with IF level / /IF blocks, so one template renders different anchor structures per level and any fix must be rendered and validated per level.

A fresh scaffold deliberately writes packet_pointer: scaffold/<slug> in document frontmatter as a not-yet-filed marker; the disk-consistency helper tolerates it in specific states, so a packet that never receives a save or repair keeps a pointer that is not its real path.

The same sample records correct paths at creation: description.json specFolder and graph-metadata.json spec_folder both name the real path, so creation is accurate and the later move (archive/restore) plus the unsaved scaffold pointer are the two drift producers.

The nested anchor is semantically wrong even if nesting were legal: the Level 2 close lands after the Open Questions items, so name-based anchor extraction returns non-functional requirements, edge cases and complexity as well as the questions section.

direction: Treating anchor defects as author error
reason: The pre-edit scaffold sample already violates the no-nesting rule with zero human edits.

direction: Fixing rendered packets without fixing the template
reason: The next scaffold would reintroduce the defect and force the corpus repair to run forever.
